text: Ordered an m&m McFlurry using a kiosk with English selected as the language. At no point did it indicate that there would be peanuts in the McFlurry as the title of the item was 'Regular McFlurry - M&M'. Upon getting the order, my girlfriend took the first bite of the McFlurry and noticed it had peanuts, which is very fortunate as if I had taken the first bite or she had not noticed I would have gone into anaphylactic shock. We returned to the McDonalds asking for them to make us an Oreo one and that they should really ensure that an item containing peanuts is clear about that allergen - especially something that normally would not like M&Ms. Both the worker at the register and the manager who she went and got gave us attitude as though we were fools for not knowing that all McFlurries in the Netherlands have peanuts and they very begrudgingly made us a terrible Oreo mcflurry which they did not attempt to mix at all. I would highly advice against going to this McDonalds and instead spend your money somewhere will they will at least treat you with a bit of respect in the event that you're trying to avoid death.
author: Jonah Fairweather

text:
Visited two nights in a row and had issues both times. First night, I wanted to dine in, but was told no trays are given out in the evening, only a paper bag — awkward and messy for dine-in.
Second night, I tried to return a reusable cup to get my €1 deposit back, but they refused because I hadn’t bought it that same evening. I explained another McDonald’s told me returns are accepted at any location since you ordered to-go, but the manager insisted it’s their policy to prevent “homeless people cashing in cups.” He said as a private franchise, they can make their own rules.
Not only was the reasoning off-putting, but the attitude was dismissive and unhelpful, I dropped it and left since it is only one euro but at the same time is only one euro why did they feel the need to fight me on this.
I read other reviews that report similar issues here — poor service, dine-in orders in bags, and confusion around cup deposits. Policies feel made up on the spot.
Would not recommend McDonalds in Amsterdam.
author: Brian Sanchez

text:
I am reaching out to share a recent experience at the McDonald's branch in Amsterdam's city center, which I believe highlights areas for improvement in customer service. During my visit, I ordered a Happy Meal but found no option for a cheeseburger. Upon addressing this at the counter, the staff mentioned it was not possible to modify the sandwich, which I understand is within policy. However, when I placed a new order for a sandwich with added lettuce, the employee's behavior was notably unprofessional. She left abruptly, returned to complete the order, but did not include the requested lettuce.

The interaction was disappointing, as I do not expect to pay for a second sandwich, wait again, and experience unkind treatment. Such behavior does not align with the standards I associate with McDonald's and reflects poorly on the brand.

I kindly suggest reviewing this branch's customer service practices to ensure a more positive experience for future patrons.

Looking forward to your response.
author: Abdullah Al-Habib

text:
I ordered a hamburger based on its shape, and didn’t check which was its name since I was in hurry.
The printer of self order did not work, and it did not give me receipt.
When I explained them that there is problem in the printer and i showed my payment in my Dutch bank account, they hesitate to give me my order. They waisted my time a lot to give me my order, I never and never order from this brand. After my order the manager ( an Indian man put new paper in printer ). Is this correct behaviour on the condition that your printer has problem and I am showing my bank transaction with its time that prove I had order this branch of Mac Donald ?????
I will send a complaint to McDonald, since your behaviour was fully impolite just for 8 euros!

text:
We were very tired from visiting Amsterdam, and sat down to eat. We had to order on consoles, only two men working in the kitchen. No time to answer questions.
When we wanted to go to the toilet, there was not any. That is forbidden by law for such an establishment!!
We were directed to Mc Donalds in the Nieuwstraat, and there we had to pay. The foreign cleaner said everybody had to pay 1,5 Euro for the toilet. As I protested that is is against the law, the foreigner working there admitted us without us having to pay.

Mc Donald's is a tourist trap, and a scam. To be avoided!
It seems that you can avoid  having to offer a toilet to your customers just by asking an exaggerated amount of money!
author: Paula V

text:
Absolutely filthy.

This was one of the worst McDonald’s experiences I’ve ever had. On a typical Sunday afternoon, trash was overflowing from the bins and scattered around them. There was spilled Coke across the floor, and food littered the kitchen area.

The food itself was dry and tasted like it had been sitting out for a while.

Worst of all, the food preparation area was a mess. Lettuce and other toppings were scattered across the counter, and I watched as one staff member gathered it all with his bare hands, threw it in the trash, wiped his hands on his pants, and then continued making food without washing them.

This location is in serious need of attention and improvement.
author: Ari Ljunggren

text:
